settings.expectations.heading: Post-apply checks
settings.expectations.help: Expectations defined on a proxy host (its
settings.expectations.help_after: section) run right after every config sync. Choose what happens when one fails.
settings.expectations.rollback_help: Load the previous live config back into Caddy, pause automatic syncs for that server, and show a banner until you re-apply or keep the rolled-back config. Off = report only: results still appear on each host's health page and in the Activity log, but the new config stays live.
settings.general.activity_retention_help: Auto-delete activity log entries older than this many days. 0 keeps all entries.
settings.general.auto_sync_help: CaddyUI re-syncs all Caddy servers automatically when this many hours have passed since the last sync. Useful as a failsafe when cert renewals or external config changes need to be reapplied.
settings.general.color_theme_help: Independent of the light/dark toggle in the top bar — both can be combined (e.g. "dark + carbon orange"). Synced to your account, so it follows you across browsers and devices.
settings.general.fallback_html_help: Leave blank to use Caddy's default error response (CaddyUI's branded page on HTTPS for 404).
settings.general.fallback_html_hint: (optional — shown with the fallback status for requests matching no proxy, redirect or Advanced route)
settings.general.fallback_status_help: Answered for a request that matches no proxy host, redirection or Advanced route — on HTTP and HTTPS alike

settings.general.maintenance_help: When enabled, ALL proxy hosts immediately serve a 503 maintenance page regardless of individual host settings. Use for emergency maintenance windows. Applied on next sync.
settings.general.site_title_help: Shown in the browser tab title and sidebar. Leave blank to use "CaddyUI".

settings.general.strip_headers_help: CaddyUI deletes these response headers from every upstream's reply on every proxy host. Concatenated with each host's own

settings.title: Settings
settings.security.captcha.title: CAPTCHA protection
settings.security.captcha.override_title: CADDYUI_CAPTCHA_DISABLE is set — challenge is bypassed regardless of the provider below
settings.security.captcha.description: Applied to sign-in, TOTP verification, and new-user creation. Pick a provider you already have an account with — Turnstile is free and privacy-friendly; reCAPTCHA is a good fallback if Cloudflare is having an outage.
settings.security.captcha.override_help: is set in the container env, so no challenge is shown or verified. Remove or unset that env var and restart to re-enable the provider below.
settings.security.captcha.off_help: No challenge. Fine for private/LAN-only deployments.
settings.security.captcha.recaptcha_inst: . Pick reCAPTCHA v3 (score-based) — v2 is not supported here.
settings.security.captcha.score_help_int: Challenges below this score are rejected. Google recommends
settings.security.captcha.score_help_end: as a starting point; raise it if you still see bot traffic, lower it if legit users are bouncing.
settings.security.policy.title: Security policy
settings.security.policy.description: Authentication requirements applied to all users.
settings.security.trusted_proxies.label: Trusted proxy IPs/CIDRs
settings.security.trusted_proxies.help: One per line or comma-separated. Used to extract real client IPs from X-Forwarded-For headers (e.g. Cloudflare, load balancers). IP allowlists and blocklists then check that real address. Only list proxies you control: anything listed here can claim any client address.
settings.security.client_headers.label: Client IP headers
settings.security.client_headers.help: Checked in order after the direct peer matches Trusted proxy IPs/CIDRs. Caddy defaults to X-Forwarded-For; Cloudflare users can put CF-Connecting-IP first.
settings.security.certificate_roots.help: One absolute path per line. CaddyUI only opens certificate and key files inside these directories — for the expiry column, Inspect, and fleet copy-by-value. Caddy loads certificates itself, so a file outside them still serves normally; it just shows as unreadable here. Add a directory only if your certificates are mounted somewhere unusual.
settings.security.disable_http3.label: Disable HTTP/3 (QUIC)
settings.security.disable_http3.help: Restricts Caddy to HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 only. Fixes "proxy mismatch" or certificate errors on older Android clients (Bitwarden, Chrome). Requires a Caddy reload to take effect.
settings.security.allowlist.label: Admin panel IP allowlist
settings.security.allowlist.help: ⚠️ One IP or CIDR per line. When set, only listed IPs can access CaddyUI.
settings.security.allowlist.warning: Make sure your own IP is included before saving!
settings.security.allowlist.forwarded_he: Read from a forwarding header, because the machine that opened this connection is a trusted proxy. This is the address the allowlist checks — include it, or a range containing it.
settings.security.allowlist.direct_help: This is the address of the connection itself, and what the allowlist checks.
settings.security.allowlist.proxy_warnin: If CaddyUI sits behind a reverse proxy and this looks like the proxy rather than your own address
settings.security.allowlist.proxy_help: above first — otherwise every visitor arrives as this one address and the allowlist cannot tell them apart.
settings.security.allowlist.placeholder:
Leave blank to allow all IPs
192.168.1.0/24
10.0.0.1
settings.security.allowlist.override_hel: is set on this container and takes precedence over the list above, which is saved but not in force. Remove the variable to go back to using it.
settings.security.allowlist.recovery_mid: in your compose file and restart — it overrides this list, and
settings.security.allowlist.recovery_end: disables the gate entirely while you get back in. What you saved here is left untouched.
settings.security.blocklist.label: Global IP blocklist
settings.security.blocklist.help_intro: One IP or CIDR per line (or comma-separated). Blocked with
settings.security.blocklist.help_middle: across every host, ahead of routing — the fleet-wide counterpart to a host's own blocklist. Populated by the
settings.security.blocklist.help_end: action on a visitor's analytics page; remove entries here to unblock.
settings.security.oidc.label: Single sign-on (OIDC)
settings.security.oidc.help: Let admins sign in through an external identity provider (Authelia, Authentik, Keycloak, Google, …) alongside local password + TOTP. Register CaddyUI as a confidential client and set its redirect URL to the callback below.
settings.security.oidc.auto_create_help: Provision a user on first SSO sign-in (verified email required). Off = only users that already exist in CaddyUI can sign in via SSO.
settings.security.oidc.role_user: User — can manage their own resources
settings.security.oidc.default_role_help: Given to a new SSO account when no group rule below matches. Existing accounts keep the role they already have — this only applies at creation.
settings.security.oidc.rules_end: , so put the most privileged first. Group names are matched case-insensitively; a rule naming an unknown role is ignored rather than guessed at.
settings.security.session.label: Session duration (days)
settings.security.session.help: New sessions will use this duration. Existing sessions are not affected.
settings.security.login_attempts.label: Max Login Attempts (per IP)
settings.security.login_attempts.help: Blocks an IP after this many failed login attempts in a 15-minute window. 0 disables brute-force protection.
settings.security.totp.help: Site-wide policy. Any user who has not enrolled TOTP is sent to the setup page and cannot reach the rest of CaddyUI until they finish. It does not enrol anyone for you, and it cannot switch TOTP on or off for one account — each person manages their own under {profile}.
settings.security.totp.warning: This applies to you too. If your own account has no TOTP yet, saving this sends you straight to enrolment, and you will need to finish it before you can reach this page again — including to switch the policy back off.
settings.security.oidc.redirect_help: Register this exact URL with your provider — including the {suffix} on the end:
settings.security.oidc.groups_help: The ID-token claim holding the user's groups — usually {claim}. Your provider has to be configured to include it in the token. Leave blank to use the default role for everyone.
login.title: Sign in · CaddyUI
login.heading: Welcome back
login.description: Sign in to manage your Caddy routes.
login.error.sso_failed: Single sign-on failed. Try again or use your password.
login.error.sso_no_user: No CaddyUI account matches your SSO identity. Ask an admin to add you.
login.error.sso_email: Your identity provider didn't return a verified email address.
login.error.sso_domain: That account's email domain is not permitted to sign in here.
login.error.security_check: Security check failed. Please try again.
login.error.login_limit: Too many failed login attempts. Please wait 15 minutes and try again.
login.error.totp_limit: Too many failed verification attempts for this account. Please wait 15 minutes and try again.
settings.security.oidc.domains_help: One domain per line. Only verified addresses in these domains may sign in through SSO — this applies to existing accounts too, not only new ones. Subdomains are not implied: list {example} separately if you need it. Local password sign-in is unaffected.
settings.security.oidc.domains_warning: Leave blank only with a private provider.
settings.security.oidc.domains_public_he: With a public one such as Google, blank means any account in the world is accepted — and with auto-create on, each of them gets a CaddyUI account.
